mechanism_narrative: The LIFR+OSMR forced-proximity novokine (flexible_GS4 linker, ~20 Å) brings two type I cytokine receptor subunits into close apposition, enabling JAK transphosphorylation across the LIFR-OSMR heterodimer. Both receptors lack intrinsic kinase activity and signal through constitutively associated JAK1/JAK2/TYK2. Under forced co-clustering, JAK transphosphorylation is enhanced, creating amplified phosphotyrosine docking sites for STAT3 (primary), STAT1, and PTPN11/SHP2 on the receptor intracellular domains. The short GS4 linker sterically excludes large adaptors like PLCG1 (which requires wider spacing for productive docking) and IRS-family adaptors (which are not canonical for cytokine receptor signaling). The biased output is synergistic JAK-STAT3 + JAK-STAT1 + SHP2-RAS-MAPK + PI3K-AKT activation, promoting muscle structural gene expression (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN) and suppressing aged-enriched stress/inflammatory markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP, CDKN2A). This mirrors the winning pattern from past iterations where muscle structural genes go UP and aged IEGs go DOWN.
